verified_claim: Wechsler and Wells describe cigarette smoke exposure as an inflammatory trigger in COPD. Chronic smoking increases oxidative stress, which contributes to lung inflammation. Smoke-related epithelial signaling releases cytokines and chemokines that recruit inflammatory cells, including neutrophils and macrophages, sustaining airway inflammatory responses.
limitation_note: This is a narrative review describing contributory mechanisms rather than demonstrating that all smokers develop persistent airway inflammation or COPD. Other exposures and infections can trigger inflammation. Inflammatory phenotypes and susceptibility differ between individuals.
review_note: Reviewed the supplied text of Wechsler and Wells, What every clinician should know about inflammation in COPD, PMCID PMC11417604. The sections Pathological and functional airway changes in COPD and Neutrophils explicitly connect smoke exposure, oxidative stress, inflammatory mediator release and immune-cell recruitment. The evidence supports Chronic cigarette smoke exposure → Airway inflammation as a contributory causal mechanism. AI-assisted review; human confirmation pending.

provisional_claim: Candidate: persistent airway inflammation contributes to mucus hypersecretion, small-airway fibrosis and structural remodeling, increasing airway resistance and airflow obstruction.
verified_passage_locator: Pathological and functional airway changes in COPD → Pathological changes; Functional consequences; Airway inflammation in COPD → Neutrophils; Macrophages
verified_claim: The review explains that inflammatory processes contribute to mucus hypersecretion, goblet cell hyperplasia, airway remodeling and small-airway fibrosis. These pathological changes, together with epithelial and mucociliary dysfunction, increase airway resistance, air trapping and persistent airflow obstruction in COPD.
limitation_note: Airway inflammation is an important contributing mechanism but is not the only cause of airflow limitation in COPD. Alveolar destruction, loss of elastic recoil, protease-antiprotease imbalance and other structural abnormalities also contribute. The review does not establish that inflammation alone is sufficient to produce persistent airflow limitation in every individual.
review_note: Reviewed the supplied Wechsler and Wells COPD inflammation review, particularly Pathological changes, Functional consequences, Neutrophils and Macrophages. The article directly links inflammatory processes to mucus hypersecretion, airway fibrosis, structural remodeling and airflow obstruction. This supports Airway inflammation → Persistent airflow limitation in COPD as a contributory causal relationship. AI-assisted review; human confirmation pending.
